newsitem.title: USA: InVision stock jumps on FAA award news.
newsitem.headline: InVision stock jumps on FAA award news.

text.p: InVision Technologies Inc. stock jumped Friday after the company won a large piece of a $52 million Federal Aviation Administration contract for its bomb detection devices.
InVision stock jumped $6.50, or 25 percent, to $32 in early afternoon trading on Nasdaq, making it one of the market's top gainers.
Analysts said they expected others in the industry, including Magal Security Systems, to get smaller pieces of the deal.

"The fact that InVision got the lion's share is not a surprise, but the size of the contract is a bit of a surprise," said R. Robert Goldman, an analyst at brokerage Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "It's a plus for the industry and a major boost for InVision."

Goldman said the timing of the award, announced late Thursday, was a surprise. Many had expected the announcement to coincide with the release of a final White House recommendation on the detection machines due Feb. 1.
InVision's headquarters in Foster City, Calif., in the San Francisco Bay area were closed for the holidays until Jan. 2.

The White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security, headed by Vice President Al Gore, in a Sept. 9 interim report recommended the U.S. government buy significant numbers of bomb detectors for U.S. airports. The panel was set up after the explosion of TWA Flight 800 off New York July 17 which killed all 230 people aboard.
InVision's $52 million contract with the FAA calls for 54 explosive detection systems, with the first unit to be delivered in January and the remainder over 12 months.
The government has the option to buy more systems in the second year, which would boost the contract's value to $110.9 million.
John Westergaard of the Westergaard On-line Systems investment research service said Congress had appropriated $144 million so far for bomb detection devices.
"This contract is a major coup for InVision, but I would be very surprised if Magal doesn't get a piece of it also," he said. Israel-based Magal stock was unchanged at $5 in Nasdaq trading.

Among others in the group, EG&G Inc. rose 75 cents to $20.75 on the New York Stock Exchange. Vivid Technologies Inc. climbed 50 cents to $11.25 on Nasdaq, American Science & Engineerings Inc. gained 50 cents to $11.25 on the American Stock Exchange, and Thermedics slipped 50 cents to $18.50.
